name: WMIC.exe
description: The WMI command-line (WMIC) utility provides a command-line interface for WMI
summary: Execute commands and payloads on remote computers with process call create
Move laterally and deploy ransomware across a network
Identify installed antivirus products through the SecurityCenter2 namespace
Gather system, process and disk information for discovery
Change the start type of services such as the Volume Shadow Copy Service

associated_apts.name: Blue Mockingbird
associated_apts.description: Blue Mockingbird has used wmic.exe and Windows Registry modifications to set the COR_PROFILER environment variable to execute a malicious DLL whenever a process loads the.NET CLR. Blue Mockingbird has used wmic.exe to set environment variables.

associated_apts.name: Chimera
associated_apts.description: Chimera has harvested data from victim's e-mail including through execution of wmic /node:<ip> process call create "cmd /c copy c:\Users\<username>\<path>\backup.pst c:\windows\temp\backup.pst" copy "i:\<path>\<username>\My Documents\<filename>.pst" copy. Chimera has used WMIC to execute remote commands.
associated_apts.sources: NCC Group Chimera January 2021 https://web.archive.org/web/20230218064220/https://research.nccgroup.com/2021/01/12/abusing-cloud-services-to-fly-under-the-radar/; Cycraft Chimera April 2020 https://web.archive.org/web/20231214094657/https://cycraft.com/download/CyCraft-Whitepaper-Chimera_V4.1.pdf

associated_apts.name: FIN8
associated_apts.description: FIN8's malicious spearphishing payloads use WMI to launch malware and spawn `cmd.exe` execution. FIN8 has also used WMIC and the Impacket suite for lateral movement, as well as during and post compromise cleanup activities.
associated_apts.sources: FireEye Obfuscation June 2017 https://web.archive.org/web/20170923102302/https://www.fireeye.com/blog/threat-research/2017/06/obfuscation-in-the-wild.html; FireEye Know Your Enemy FIN8 Aug 2016 https://www2.fireeye.com/WBNR-Know-Your-Enemy-UNC622-Spear-Phishing.html; Bitdefender FIN8 July 2021 https://businessinsights.bitdefender.com/deep-dive-into-a-fin8-attack-a-forensic-investigation; Symantec FIN8 Jul 2023 https://symantec-enterprise-blogs.security.com/blogs/threat-intelligence/syssphinx-fin8-backdoor

associated_apts.name: MirrorFace

associated_apts.name: Naikon
associated_apts.description: Naikon has used WMIC.exe for lateral movement.

associated_apts.name: NIMBUS MANTICORE
associated_apts.description: NIMBUS MANTICORE has identified logged in users on victim hosts using `quser.exe` and `wmic.exe`. NIMBUS MANTICORE has leveraged `wmic.exe` to enumerate logged in users on compromised devices.

associated_apts.name: ToddyCat
associated_apts.description: ToddyCat can determine is Kaspersky software is running on an endpoint by running `cmd /c wmic process where name="avp.exe"`.

associated_apts.name: VOID MANTICORE

associated_apts.sources: Check Point VOID MANTICORE Handala Hack March 2026 https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/handala-hack-unveiling-groups-modus-operandi/

associated_apts.name: Volt Typhoon
associated_apts.description: Volt Typhoon has leveraged WMIC for execution, remote system discovery, and to create and use temporary directories.
associated_apts.sources: CISA AA24-038A PRC Critical Infrastructure February 2024 https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/2024-03/aa24-038a_csa_prc_state_sponsored_actors_compromise_us_critical_infrastructure_3.pdf; Secureworks BRONZE SILHOUETTE May 2023 https://web.archive.org/web/20230601025540/https://www.secureworks.com/blog/chinese-cyberespionage-group-bronze-silhouette-targets-us-government-and-defense-organizations; Microsoft Volt Typhoon May 2023 https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2023/05/24/volt-typhoon-targets-us-critical-infrastructure-with-living-off-the-land-techniques/; Joint Cybersecurity Advisory Volt Typhoon June 2023 https://media.defense.gov/2023/May/24/2003229517/-1/-1/0/CSA_Living_off_the_Land.PDF

associated_apts.name: Wizard Spider
associated_apts.description: Wizard Spider has used WMI and LDAP queries for network discovery and to move laterally. Wizard Spider has also used batch scripts to leverage WMIC to deploy ransomware. Wizard Spider has used batch scripts that utilizes WMIC to execute a BITSAdmin transfer of a ransomware payload to each compromised machine. Wizard Spider has used WMIC and vssadmin to manually delete volume shadow copies. Wizard Spider has also used Conti ransomware to delete volume shadow copies automatically with the use of vssadmin.
associated_apts.sources: Red Canary Hospital Thwarted Ryuk October 2020 https://redcanary.com/blog/how-one-hospital-thwarted-a-ryuk-ransomware-outbreak/; DHS/CISA Ransomware Targeting Healthcare October 2020 https://us-cert.cisa.gov/ncas/alerts/aa20-302a; CrowdStrike Grim Spider May 2019 https://www.crowdstrike.com/blog/timelining-grim-spiders-big-game-hunting-tactics/; FireEye KEGTAP SINGLEMALT October 2020 https://www.fireeye.com/blog/threat-research/2020/10/kegtap-and-singlemalt-with-a-ransomware-chaser.html; Mandiant FIN12 Oct 2021 https://web.archive.org/web/20220313061955/https://www.mandiant.com/sites/default/files/2021-10/fin12-group-profile.pdf

associated_campaigns.name: C0015
associated_campaigns.description: During C0015, the threat actors used `wmic` and `rundll32` to load Cobalt Strike onto a target host.

associated_campaigns.name: C0018
associated_campaigns.description: During C0018, the threat actors used WMIC to modify administrative settings on both a local and a remote host, likely as part of the first stages for their lateral movement; they also used WMI Provider Host (`wmiprvse.exe`) to execute a variety of encoded PowerShell scripts using the `DownloadString` method.
associated_campaigns.sources: Costa AvosLocker May 2022 https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/raas-avoslocker-incident-response-analysis-fl%C3%A1vio-costa?trk=articles_directory; Cisco Talos Avos Jun 2022 https://blog.talosintelligence.com/avoslocker-new-arsenal/

associated_campaigns.name: Operation Dream Job
associated_campaigns.description: During Operation Dream Job, Lazarus Group used WMIC to executed a remote XSL script.

associated_malware.name: Action RAT
associated_malware.description: Action RAT can identify AV products on an infected host using the following command: `cmd.exe WMIC /Node:localhost /Namespace:\root\SecurityCenter2 Path AntiVirusProduct Get displayName /Format:List`.

associated_malware.name: Astaroth
associated_malware.description: Astaroth uses WMIC to execute payloads.

associated_malware.name: Avaddon
associated_malware.description: Avaddon uses wmic.exe to delete shadow copies.

associated_malware.name: BlackCat
associated_malware.description: BlackCat can delete shadow copies using `vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet` and `wmic.exe Shadowcopy Delete`; it can also modify the boot loader using `bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No`. BlackCat can use `wmic.exe` to delete shadow copies on compromised networks.

associated_malware.name: CharmPower
associated_malware.description: CharmPower can use `wmic` to gather information from a system.

associated_malware.name: IcedID
associated_malware.description: IcedID can identify AV products on an infected host using the following command: ` WMIC.exe WMIC /Node:localhost /Namespace:\root\SecurityCenter2 Path AntiVirusProduct Get * /Format:List`.

associated_malware.name: INC Ransomware
associated_malware.description: INC Ransomware has the ability to use wmic.exe to spread to multiple endpoints within a compromised environment.
associated_malware.sources: Secureworks GOLD IONIC April 2024 https://www.secureworks.com/blog/gold-ionic-deploys-inc-ransomware; Huntress INC Ransom Group August 2023 https://www.huntress.com/blog/investigating-new-inc-ransom-group-activity

associated_malware.name: jRAT
associated_malware.description: jRAT can list security software, such as by using WMIC to identify anti-virus products installed on the victim’s machine and to obtain firewall details. jRAT uses WMIC to identify anti-virus products installed on the victim’s machine and to obtain firewall details.
associated_malware.sources: jRAT Symantec Aug 2018 https://www.symantec.com/blogs/threat-intelligence/jrat-new-anti-parsing-techniques; Kaspersky Adwind Feb 2016 https://media.kasperskycontenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/43/2018/03/07195002/KL_AdwindPublicReport_2016.pdf

associated_malware.name: KOCTOPUS
associated_malware.description: KOCTOPUS has checked the OS version using `wmic.exe` and the `find` command.

associated_malware.name: LAMEHUG
associated_malware.description: LAMEHUG can use wmic to collect system information.

associated_malware.name: LockBit 2.0
associated_malware.description: LockBit 2.0 can use wmic.exe to delete volume shadow copies.

associated_malware.name: Meteor
associated_malware.description: Meteor can use `wmic.exe` as part of its effort to delete shadow copies. Meteor can use `bcdedit` to delete different boot identifiers on a compromised host; it can also use `vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet` and `C:\Windows\system32\wbem\wmic.exe shadowcopy delete`.

associated_malware.name: NotPetya
associated_malware.description: NotPetya can use wmic to help propagate itself across a network. NotPetya can use valid credentials with PsExec or wmic to spread itself to remote systems. NotPetya uses rundll32.exe to install itself on remote systems when accessed via PsExec or wmic.

associated_malware.name: Octopus
associated_malware.description: Octopus has used wmic.exe for local discovery information.

associated_malware.name: ProLock
associated_malware.description: ProLock can use WMIC to execute scripts on targeted hosts.

associated_malware.name: PUBLOAD
associated_malware.description: PUBLOAD has leveraged `wmic logicaldisk get` to map local network drives. PUBLOAD has used `wmic` to gather information from the victim device. PUBLOAD has identified AV products on an infected host using the following command: `WMIC /Node:localhost /Namespace:\root\SecurityCenter2 Path AntiVirusProduct Get displayName /Format:List`.
associated_malware.sources: Trend Micro MUSTANG PANDA PUBLOAD HIUPAN SEPTEMBER 2024 https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/24/i/earth-preta-new-malware-and-strategies.html

associated_malware.name: PyDCrypt
associated_malware.description: PyDCrypt has attempted to execute with WMIC.

associated_malware.name: Qilin
associated_malware.description: Qilin can use WMIC to change the Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) startup type to manual.

associated_malware.name: Raspberry Robin
associated_malware.description: Raspberry Robin can execute via LNK containing a command to run a legitimate executable, such as wmic.exe, to download a malicious Windows Installer (MSI) package.

associated_malware.name: Remexi
associated_malware.description: Remexi executes received commands with wmic.exe (for WMI commands).

associated_malware.name: StoneDrill
associated_malware.description: StoneDrill has used the WMI command-line (WMIC) utility to run tasks.

associated_malware.name: The Gentlemen Ransomware
associated_malware.description: The Gentlemen Ransomware has deleted Volume Shadow Copies through the use of `vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet` and `wmic shadowcopy delete`. The Gentlemen Ransomware has also inhibited system recovery by stopping backup services, disabling endpoint protection agents and remote access tools. The Gentlemen Ransomware has utilized wmic to execute commands on victim devices. The Gentlemen Ransomware has also leveraged WMI to enumerate volumes and drives.

associated_malware.name: Valak
associated_malware.description: Valak can use wmic process call create in a scheduled task to launch plugins and for execution.

associated_malware.name: WannaCry
associated_malware.description: WannaCry uses vssadmin, wbadmin, bcdedit, and wmic to delete and disable operating system recovery features. WannaCry utilizes wmic to delete shadow copies.
associated_malware.sources: FireEye WannaCry 2017 https://www.fireeye.com/blog/threat-research/2017/05/wannacry-malware-profile.html; SecureWorks WannaCry Analysis https://www.secureworks.com/research/wcry-ransomware-analysis; LogRhythm WannaCry https://web.archive.org/web/20230522041200/https://logrhythm.com/blog/a-technical-analysis-of-wannacry-ransomware/

associated_malware.name: Zebrocy
associated_malware.description: Zebrocy uses the tasklist and wmic process get Capture, ExecutablePath commands to gather the processes running on the system.

associated_commands.intent: Inhibit recovery: BlackCat deletes volume shadow copies.
Discovery: BlackCat reads the device UUID of the target machine.

associated_commands.command: wmic /node:"<node>" /user:"<user>" /password:"!Secure4u123!" process call create "cmd.exe /c copy \\<node>\c$\windows\temp\<redacted>.exe c:\windows\temp\"
associated_commands.intent: Ransomware deployment: copy the encryption executable onto each remote endpoint over WMI, with stolen credentials.
Discovery: the dropped Go binary checks which domain the compromised host belongs to.

associated_commands.command: cmd /c start /b wmic diskdrive where Name="\\.\PHYSICALDRIVE0" get model,name,SerialNumber >> c:\users\public\d
associated_commands.intent: Discovery during lateral movement: record the model, name and serial number of the remote host's first disk.

associated_commands.command: cmd /c wmic process where name="avp.exe" get processid,executablepath,name,creationdate,CommandLine >> C:\users\public\d
associated_commands.intent: Check whether Kaspersky's endpoint agent (avp.exe) is running on the remote host.

associated_commands.command: cmd.exe /c "wmic product get name, InstallLocation, InstallDate, Version /format:csv > $FilePath"
associated_commands.intent: Discovery: the CharmPower toolkit lists installed programs with their versions and install paths.
Run the dropped IcedID loader with regsvr32 through WMI, started from the malicious Excel document.
Discovery: IcedID lists the installed antivirus products right after it checks in.

associated_commands.command: wmic /node:"<IP ADDRESS>" /user:"<DOMAIN>\Administrator" /password:"<PASSWORD>" process call create "cmd.exe /c c:\windows\temp\ttsel.exe"
associated_commands.intent: Ransomware deployment: start the Quantum payload on remote hosts over WMI with stolen administrator credentials.
Lateral movement: NotPetya runs its DLL on other hosts through WMI with recovered credentials.
Fingerprint the victim: the Octopus Trojan reads the computer name to build a victim ID.
Discovery: list programs that start automatically, part of PUBLOAD's network mapping commands.
associated_commands.source_name: Trend Micro MUSTANG PANDA PUBLOAD HIUPAN SEPTEMBER 2024

associated_commands.command: cmd /C wmic service where name='vss' call ChangeStartMode Manual
associated_commands.intent: Inhibit recovery: set the Volume Shadow Copy service to manual start before deleting all shadow copies.

associated_commands.command: cmd.exe /C wmic product where Name like '%kaspe%' get Name, IdentifyingNumber
associated_commands.intent: Check whether Kaspersky products are installed while the ransomware spreads across hosts.
The attackers used the WMI command-line tool to list the compromised system's running processes, which are sent to the C&C server.
Zebrocy sends commands to the victim to collect system information, including the process list with wmic.

associated_commands.command: cmd /c cd /d C:\inetpub\wwwroot\aspnet_client\system_web&wmic process where name=smex_master.exe get ExecutablePath,commandline&echo [S]&cd&echo [E]
associated_commands.intent: The attacker enumerated further information about specific processes on the victim system, here the Trend Micro ScanMail process smex_master.exe.
The actor performs initial reconnaissance using WMI, here querying the last boot time.

associated_commands.command: wmic product where name="CarbonBlack Sensor" call uninstall /nointeractive
associated_commands.intent: UNC2165 scripts used WMI to uninstall anti-virus products and stop services before ransomware deployment.
After the Falcon platform blocked their PowerShell scripts, the adversary tried to diagnose the failure with this command and tasklist.
StoneDrill runs a dropped VBS script through WMIC to copy itself into the %COMMON_APPDATA%\Chrome folder.
During lateral movement the attackers ran their Cobalt Strike DLL through rundll32 started by WMIC.

associated_commands.command: wmic.exe /node:[REDACTED_HOSTNAME] /user:[REDACTED] /password:[REDACTED] process call create "cmd.exe /c copy \\?\GLOBALROOT\Device\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy1\windows\system32\config\system c:\users\public”
associated_commands.intent: During credential extraction the attacker used WMIC to copy the SYSTEM hive from a volume shadow copy on a remote host.
associated_commands.source_name: Check Point Handala Modus Operandi March 2026

associated_commands.intent: On the Domain Controller the threat actors gathered information about the installed security software through WMI.
associated_commands.source_name: The DFIR Report Qbot and Zerologon February 2022

associated_commands.intent: To use COR_PROFILER persistence, the actor used wmic.exe and Registry modifications to set environment variables and specify a DLL payload.
Listed as an example of a command used for lateral movement in the compromised network.
The report shows APT41 using WMIC to run a payload on a remote host (Windows Management Instrumentation, T1047).
The jRAT payload uses a WMIC interface to identify the antivirus products installed on the compromised computer.
The Octopus Trojan runs WMIC.exe to build the victim fingerprint id, here reading the OS install date.
LunarWeb discovers installed security solutions via this WMI query.

associated_commands.command: C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe /c wmic.exe /node:localhost /namespace:\\root\SecurityCenter2 path AntiVirusProduct Get DisplayName | findstr /V /B /C:displayName || echo No Antivirus installed
associated_commands.intent: The LATRODECTUS command handler runs system discovery commands, including this wmic antivirus query, and sends the output to the C2.
The C# Zebrocy variant gathers system information with WMI queries run through wmic instead of systeminfo and tasklist.

associated_commands.command: C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe /C WMIC/node:"DC.DOMAIN.local" process call create "cmd /c C:\PerfLogs\servisess.exe\"
associated_commands.intent: After copying an executable to the domain controller over SMB, the threat actors used WMI from the beachhead host to execute it.
associated_commands.source_name: The DFIR Report Ryuk in 5 Hours October 2020

associated_commands.intent: A batch file queried target hosts with WMIC to determine the host disk drive configuration, including mounted network shares.
associated_commands.source_name: The DFIR Report Malicious ISO to Ransomware April 2023

associated_commands.intent: The beacon launched this command during system information and software discovery.
After AD discovery the threat actors used WMI to gather information about Windows OS version and licensing on remote hosts.
associated_commands.source_name: The DFIR Report IcedID Nokoyawa May 2023

associated_commands.command: C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe /C wmic /node:<REDACTED> process call create "cmd /C > C:\ProgramData\1.txt 2>&1 reg query HKEY_USERS\<SID>\Network"
associated_commands.intent: The attackers saved the list of mapped shares of a remote host to a text file by running reg query through wmic.
associated_commands.source_name: The DFIR Report Truebot Graceful Wipe-Out June 2023

associated_commands.intent: The actor ran this command to gather information about local drives.
associated_commands.source_name: NSA/CISA PRC Actor Living off the Land June 2023
